title: Let's integrate AI Agents in Event-Sourced Systems — Divakar Kumar, FlyersSoft
talk_summary: A fraud-detection team keeps their existing rule/ML tier-1 engine and adds a tier-2 agentic layer only for the uncertain 'gray zone', feeding agents from a denormalized semantic/projection layer built off event-sourced contexts. They fan out to two specialist agents (risk, behavior) and use a third verdict agent to reconcile them instead of a numeric threshold, then emit the verdict back as an event into saga orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Tiered escalation: cheap deterministic gate first, agents only on the ambiguous residue
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the existing rule/ML engine as tier-1 handling the clear approve/block cases; route only gray-zone cases to the agentic tier-2 layer, so agents are invoked rarely and only where they add value.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most of the cases would be handled really well by these existing system... we are just trying to handle few of the areas like that is the gray zone areas with the help of agentic AI

takeaways.technique: Semantic/projection layer as the single context source for agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of agents querying many bounded contexts live, they build a denormalized materialized view (counts, averages, device trust, KYC status, recent payments) via CDC/message broker, and expose it to agents only through narrow tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you need to just create the semantic layer for you to provide enough context to these AI agents

takeaways.technique: Fan-out to specialist agents + a reconciling verdict agent instead of a scalar threshold
takeaways.what_they_do: Fan the event to a risk agent and a behavior agent in parallel, then a third agent reads both outputs and decides, because a plain numeric threshold reintroduced the false positives of the old rule engine.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we are using just the metrics, it is again going back to the same criteria... there are many false positive cases... we are trying to use a third agent in this verdict layer

takeaways.technique: Explicit loop-termination metrics per use case
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent loop decomposes tasks and iterates until goal reached, but they define metrics/thresholds beyond which the loop is forcibly broken to avoid infinite loops.

takeaways.technique: Short-term in-memory state only, sized to the SLA
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately use in-memory short-term memory rather than long-term memory because the transaction SLA is sub-500ms, trading memory richness for latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we are using an inch um short memory because... it should be sub 500 milliseconds... we are currently using in-memory for this

takeaways.technique: Small/open models acceptable for agent components
takeaways.what_they_do: They note the agent's language model need not be a large model — an SLM or open-source model can serve, implying model choice is a per-component cost lever.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this language model it it is not necessary to be a large language model. It could be a SLM. It could be an open-source model
